title: Why Should Cross and Trial Grieve Me?
alsoKnownAs: Why Should Sorrow Ever Grieve Me?
description: Why Should Cross and Trial Grieve Me? in Tonic Solfa: the solfa line by line with the words, staff notation, all 5 verses, and a piano to sing along with.
about: The words are by Paul Gerhardt, first published in 1653. The English translation is by John Kelly (1867). The tune, EBELING, is by Johann Georg Ebeling (1666). This version of the melody and the words comes from the Open Hymnal Project.
underlay: Why should cross and tri-al grieve me? Christ is near With His cheer; Ne-ver will He leave me. Who can rob me of the hea-ven That God's Son, For my own, To my faith hath gi-ven?

lines: Why should cross and trial grieve me?
Who can rob me of the heaven
Nought not e'en the life I'm living,
Must I then His own restore Him?
Though a heavy cross I'm bearing,
God can help me, who doth send it,
And how best to end it.
God oft gives me days of gladness,
God is good, and tempers ever
Let them now employ their jeering,
